en: Petavatthu, Cūḷavagga, 6. Seriṇīpetivatthu The Story of the Seriṇī Ghost Once upon a time, there was a woman named Seriṇī who lived in the city of Sāvatthī. She was beautiful, virtuous, and well-versed in the Dhamma. Having passed away, she was reborn as a female ghost (petī) in the realm of ghosts. One day, while wandering through the air, she saw the Blessed One sitting surrounded by a great assembly of monks. Desiring to see the Teacher, she approached him. Seeing her from afar, the Blessed One said to the monks: "Monks, do you see that female ghost approaching? She was once a human being in this very city of Sāvatthī. Because she was virtuous and well-versed in the Dhamma, she has now been reborn in the company of the devas. When the monks heard this, they were filled with wonder and asked the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, what deeds did she perform to be reborn thus? The Blessed One replied: "Monks, in her previous life, this woman was a lay follower in Sāvatthī. She was faithful, virtuous, and devoted to the Triple Gem. Whenever she saw monks, she would offer them food, robes, and other requisites. Furthermore, she took delight in listening to the Dhamma and would often recite the teachings to others. Because of these meritorious deeds, she has now been reborn in the realm of the devas. Having heard this, the monks were inspired and paid homage to the Blessed One. The Blessed One then taught them the Dhamma, and at the end of the discourse, many attained the fruits of stream-entry and beyond. Thus ends the story of the Seriṇī ghost. May all beings be happy. “Naked, of ugly form,
emaciated, with veins showing all over;
you are parched, you are thin.”
“Who are you that stands here?
“I am a peta, venerable sir,
miserable and belonging to the world of Yama.”
“Having committed evil deeds,
they have gone from here to the world of the petas.
“What indeed [did they do] by way of body or speech?”
“An evil deed was committed by you with the mind;
as the ripening of what karma have you gone from here to the world of petas?”
“While there were open fords,
he sought one for half a māsaka;
while there were things to be given, [he sought them].”
I made no lamp for myself.
Thirsty, I approach the river,
but it flows back empty.
I approach the shade when it is hot,
and the sunlight shifts away;
even the wind has the color of fire to me.
It burns as it blows upon me;
Venerable Sir, I deserve this and other evils even worse than that.
Having gone to the city,
he addressed the female elephant, my mother:
"Your daughter has been seen by me."
Destitute and belonging to the world of Yama,
having committed evil deeds,
they have gone from here to the realm of the departed spirits.
There is something deposited here by me that has not yet been explained:
four hundred thousand [verses].
And from beneath my throne,
let her give alms to me,
and let that be her means of livelihood.
And having given a gift, may my mother dedicate the merit to me;
then I shall be happy.
“Fulfilling all desires.
Having agreed, saying “Very well,” he went to the city of the female elephant.
He said to her mother:
"I have seen your daughter,
fallen into misfortune in the world of Yama."
Having committed an evil deed, she has gone from here to the world of the departed.
There, she incited me [to do the same]. (…)
He sent word to my mother:
"Your daughter has been seen by me,
fallen into misfortune in the world of Yama."
Having committed evil deeds,
they have gone from here to the world of the petas;
and there is something deposited by me here.
And that was not declared by me;
there were four hundred thousand [treasures] beneath the cross-legged seat.
Therefore, let her give alms to me,
and let that be her livelihood;
and having given alms to me, my mother—
“May he accept my offering;
then I shall be happy,
with all my desires fulfilled.”
For she gave that gift and dedicated the merit to him;
and the female spirit became happy.
"And her life was well-lived.
This is the sixth story, the Story of Seriṇī.
